title: Yang–Mills Mass Gap on the Lattice and One Cube from the Continuum
description: Source, programs and Lean 4 certificate of the paper Yang–Mills Mass Gap on the Lattice and One Cube from the Continuum, by Deep Bhattacharjee, Ushashi Bhattacharya, James Montgomery Lockwood and Tristan Romanov (Hexagon preprint 2610.00341). The gauge of four-dimensional lattice Yang–Mills theory is fixed on a period-two field of straight lines that meets every plaquette in exactly one link. At fixed lattice spacing this gives a unique free-boundary state, reflection positivity, exponential clustering and an explicit transfer-matrix gap: for SU(2) up to beta_W = 0.351 and for SU(3) up to beta_W = 0.77 through plaquette blocks with constants certified in ball arithmetic, and for every compact simple group G when N|beta| < 2 kappa_G/29, with kappa_G = h^vee/(2 l_rho) the least Ricci curvature, extended to 2 kappa_G/28.840002 by a certificate for the gauge-fixed Hessian. The continuum step is reduced to one cube: a Dobrushin–Shlosman condition on a cube of fixed physical size, uniform along the continuum tuning, gives a mass gap in physical units in every continuum limit, also for observables smoothed by the spatial gradient flow. The paper proves what that cube estimate needs (a side of order (beta_W/log beta_W)^{1/4} spacings; it cannot come from single lines of links) and builds a block-averaging route towards it: a constrained quadratic gap 5000/537, a covariant cut-off of Balaban's averaging that composes on small-curvature fields and carries the SU(2) Wilson field through its large-field clusters up to that scale, effective forms local uniformly in the scale, log-concave charts of the fibres of the average with explicit decay constants for every compact group, Peierls bounds on the mass off the chart on every fibre, calm completions of every exterior along the tuning, and bounded Dobrushin response when a link is conditioned on a fixed large-field set. Coarse defects: the curvature of the block averages costs action independent of the scale; the Haar tilt bounds the tails of the force along a fixed direction by the second variation of the action at every scale and under every exterior, which makes coarse defects rare for U(1) at the rate beta_W x^2 at every scale, while for SU(2) the second variation grows like 4^k on the gauge orbit of the vacuum, and the same happens when the direction is transported along a forest, which keeps the Haar measures but leaves the residual gauge freedom of the blocks; the remaining statement is a second-variation bound on a smooth section of the gauge orbits, with its Jacobian. Lean 4 (Mathlib) checks the combinatorics of the line field and the block gauge, the finite arithmetic of the perturbation propositions, and the chain of rational bounds of the SU(2) blocks; the ball-arithmetic programs (python-flint) are included. The cube estimate along the continuum tuning and the existence of a nontrivial Osterwalder–Schrader continuum limit are not proved; the Clay Millennium problem is open. The archive also keeps the sources of two earlier papers of the project in tex/ and strong-coupling/prd/.
